findings.problem: The change says each confirmation keeps the owner's reason, but only confirm_element takes and stores one. confirm_all_proposed confirms every proposed element through the same kernel confirm_element call with no reason, and confirm_wording_element does the same for an agent. Elements confirmed either way end up confirmed with confirmation_reason unset, so the note is missing exactly where later readers would look for it. The field is optional and nothing requires it on a confirmed element, so nothing flags the gap.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml: actions confirm_all_proposed and confirm_wording_element; objects.Element.confirmation_reason

findings.problem: confirm_element now has a new required param (reason), so every existing caller that invokes it without one is broken. The domain's version stays at 4, and the composition still pins authoring interface 1, so consumers are given no signal that the action signature changed.

The new reason param has no check that it is non-empty, so an owner can confirm with a blank string. The note is then recorded but says nothing about why the element was accepted, which defeats the purpose of the change.
